tensions: Fear & Greed prints 71 (Greed) while Bitcoin sits 37% below its October 2025 high and got rejected at $82,000 for the fourth time since August 25. That divergence is the whole story: sentiment is being set by alt-coin fireworks, not by the asset that actually governs liquidity. BTC dominance at 58.9% was rejected at 60% and the Altcoin Season Index is stuck near 27 — this is not alt season, it is a handful of names with genuine catalysts running while the index bleeds. Second tension: the macro got worse, not better. A rate hike and a failed crypto bill in the same week is a hostile setup, and this book is 99.5% invested with $7.79 of cash. There is no ammunition for a drawdown and no hedge. The XRP rotation is the right trade on its merits, but it is also the only lever available, which is itself the finding.

opening.text: Book is $1,691 against $1,231 deposited — up 37.4% in seventeen days. But read the tape, not the P&L: total market cap is down 4.5% on the day, the Fed raised to 3.75-4.00% on the 16th, and the CLARITY Act died 49-50 in the Senate on the 15th. Every green line in this portfolio is idiosyncratic — NEAR's confidential TVL milestone, INJ's Solana launch, ZEC's ETF inflows, ARB's Robinhood Chain revenue. None of it is beta. That is a feature until it isn't.

NEAR is the problem child of the winners. Up 62.5% on our entry and up 67% in seven days on the back of a $70M confidential-TVL claim window and Hyperliquid perps. The catalyst is real and the catalyst is also fully in the price. We do not add. We do not trim for the sake of trimming either — the mandate says ride it. But if this book needs cash at any point next week, NEAR is where it comes from, not ZEC.

One actionable trade: sell XRP, buy ZEC. XRP is down 4.2% over six days and its entire thesis was regulatory — the CLARITY vote was the catalyst and it failed. Holding a broken thesis because the loss is small is how small losses become 14-day dead money. Proceeds of $94.33 plus the $7.79 of dry powder into ZEC on a limit at $1,450, which is a 9% pullback from Friday's $1,589 high with $358M of three-week ETF inflows and NU7 passing at 99.9% behind it. Rotating a dead catalyst into a live one beats chasing something up 67% in a week.

Watch list, not action list. XLM is dead flat at six days — day 14 is September 28, and if it hasn't moved by then it funds something else. ARB is down 7.5% but only three days old and the thesis got stronger this week, not weaker: Standard Chartered initiated with a $0.50 2026 target and the September 16 unlock has already been absorbed. The real risk to ARB is the Robinhood Chain gas subsidy ending, which nobody has priced. Buying power is $7.79 — effectively zero. Every new position in this book now requires killing an old one.
